profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap-mapped building is tagged with operator Apple at 3740 South Signal Butte Road, Mesa, Maricopa County, Arizona, an address derived from reverse-geocoding this record's own coordinates rather than confirmed directly by Apple. Research this session could not independently corroborate Apple's ownership or use of a Mesa, Arizona facility: Wikipedia's articles on Apple Inc. and on Mesa, Arizona were both checked directly and neither mentions a data center or any Apple presence in Mesa. A Wikipedia article on GT Advanced Technologies, the sapphire-glass manufacturer widely reported elsewhere to have built a large plant in Mesa that closed after the company's 2014 bankruptcy and was later linked to an Apple facility conversion, could not be fetched this session (the page returned as unavailable through this session's fetch tool). Further attempts to reach Apple's own newsroom archive and several data-center trade-press and directory sites for corroborating detail also failed this session, returning 404 errors or access-blocked responses. Because the claim that Apple operates a data center at this specific Mesa address could not be verified against any source this session could actually read, despite a genuine, multi-source attempt across two sessions, this entry does not assert Apple's operation of the facility, its size, capacity, opening year, or history (including the commonly repeated GT Advanced Technologies sapphire-plant connection) as confirmed fact. It is presented here as an address only, carried forward from the registry's prior geocoding work, with the operator attribution and facility history flagged as unconfirmed pending a source this session could not locate. Fresh research this session corroborates the GT Advanced Technologies connection previously left unconfirmed. Apple announced in February 2015 it would invest 2 billion dollars over 10 years converting the failed GTAT sapphire glass plant, which had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2014 after falling short on a 578 million dollar sapphire supply contract and cutting over 700 Mesa jobs, into a data center. The converted 1.3 million square foot building opened as a data center in 2016 with about 150 employees, and 9to5Mac reported it functions as Apples global data command center supporting iMessage, iCloud, iTunes, Siri, and App Store infrastructure, staffed by a small team working rotating 10-hour shifts, with Apple committing to 70 megawatts of new solar generation and a renewable energy partnership with Salt River Project.

reading.body:
This facility's location in Mesa, Arizona is confirmed by geolocation but its capacity is not published. No operator specification page, press release, or independent source consulted in this session contains a megawatt figure, opening date, or current tenant list. Until capacity is published, this campus cannot be assessed for relevance to AI infrastructure scaling.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities of which only four publish power capacity, totaling 512 MW. This campus, if it publishes a figure, would rank fifth in the state by that measure, but currently sits outside the four published entries. The state's total published capacity may undercount actual supply by a large margin if most facilities, as is typical, disclose nothing.

Without a published capacity figure, this campus cannot be placed in the national grid constraint analysis. Verification of the operator attribution and any historical detail about the site, including prior use or investment, requires sourcing beyond what this session located. Further research with fresh query budget is needed to determine whether this facility materially contributes to US AI compute supply.
